subject: environmental-science
title: The Nitrogen Cycle and Reactive N
welcome_lead: From N₂ inertia to NH₃ reactivity — the chemistry that feeds and pollutes.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on nitrogen fixation, nitrification and denitrification.
final_note: Haber-Bosch broke an evolutionary stalemate — now reactive nitrogen pollutes water and air.

concepts.def: Conversion of atmospheric N₂ to NH₃; biological (Rhizobium) or industrial (Haber-Bosch).
Oxidation of NH₄⁺ → NO₂⁻ → NO₃⁻ by Nitrosomonas/Nitrobacter.
Anaerobic reduction of NO₃⁻ to N₂ by Pseudomonas spp.
Microbial breakdown of organic N to NH₄⁺.
All non-N₂ forms (NOx, NH₃, NH₄⁺, NO₃⁻, organic N) biologically active.
Industrial process synthesising NH₃ from N₂ and H₂; ~150 Mt N yr⁻¹.

walkthroughs.body_html: Microbes drive the cycle: fixation captures N₂; nitrification oxidises NH₄⁺; denitrification returns N₂.
Industrial N fixation now equals natural rates, doubling reactive N flux and driving eutrophication and N₂O emissions.
Reactive N leaks into groundwater (nitrate >50 mg L⁻¹ harmful), forms tropospheric O₃, and is a potent GHG as N₂O.

mcqs.q: Why is burning fossil fuels considered to disrupt the carbon cycle?

It creates new carbon that did not exist before.
It removes carbon permanently.
Because plants only use carbon.
